title: Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch
summary: The cafeteria serves sandwiches in a stack, with students in a queue preferring either circular (0) or square (1) sandwiches.
statement: The cafeteria serves sandwiches in a stack, with students in a queue preferring either circular (0) or square (1) sandwiches. At each step, a student takes the top sandwich if it matches their preference, or moves to the end of the queue. The process continues until no student wants the top sandwich. Given the types of sandwiches and students' preferences, determine how many students cannot eat.
constraints: Students and sandwiches contain only zero and one and have equal lengths.
Students may rotate freely until nobody wants the current sandwich; return the number left.
hints: Queue rotations change order but not the count of each remaining preference.
Consume the top sandwich whenever its preference count is positive; otherwise stop.
Count zeros and ones, scan sandwiches, decrement a matching count, and return remaining total at the first zero count.
If a matching student exists rotations bring one forward; if none exists no future action can remove the top sandwich.
editorial: If a matching student exists rotations bring one forward; if none exists no future action can remove the top sandwich.

tests.explanation: Every sandwich preference can be matched, leaving zero students.
Three students remain when the next sandwich type has no interested student.
